content.text:
Welcome and password-reset emails are now wired into `src/lib/users.ts`, using **Resend**. I picked it because it has a simple API, good deliverability and works well with Next.js. I call its REST API with plain `fetch`, so no new package was added. A local test passed (details at the end); nothing has been sent through the real Resend service yet. I haven't committed anything.

**What's new**
- **`src/lib/email/send.ts`** – `sendEmail()` sends through Resend. If `RESEND_API_KEY` isn't set, it prints the email to the console instead, so you can work locally without an account. In production a missing key is an error.
- **`src/lib/email/templates.ts`** – the welcome and password-reset emails, each in an HTML and a plain-text version. User-supplied values are escaped in the HTML.
- **`src/lib/users.ts`**:
  - `createUser({ email, name })` cleans up and lowercases the email, rejects duplicates, then sends the welcome email. If that email fails, it's logged and signup still succeeds.
  - `requestPasswordReset(email)` creates a random token that expires after 60 minutes and emails a link to `${APP_URL}/reset-password?token=…`. Only a hash of the token is stored, and a new request cancels any earlier link. For an unknown email it does nothing and returns normally, so it doesn't reveal which emails have accounts.
  - `consumePasswordResetToken(token)` checks the token and returns the matching user. It's one-use: it's deleted after the first check.
  - I also added `getUserByEmail` as a helper.
- **`.env.example`** – placeholders for `RESEND_API_KEY`, `EMAIL_FROM`, `EMAIL_REPLY_TO` and `APP_URL`. I changed `.gitignore` so this file can be committed; it was ignored by the default `.env*` rule.

**Testing:** lint passes. TypeScript reports one error, in the existing `src/app/layout.tsx` (a `LayoutProps` type that Next generates during a build); none come from the new code. With no API key set, I created a user and checked that the welcome email was printed. I then asked for a reset, used the token from the printed link, and confirmed that it found the right user and that a second use was rejected. A reset request for an unknown email sent nothing.

**Still to do**
- **Live sending:** you need a real `RESEND_API_KEY`, and `EMAIL_FROM` must be on a domain you've verified in Resend.
- **No pages or password storage yet:** there is no signup form, "forgot password" page, or `/reset-password` page. The user model also has no password field, so `consumePasswordResetToken` only confirms who the user is; whatever sets the new password should call it.
- **Data is in memory:** users and reset tokens are lost on restart, like the existing user list. Once there's a database, both need to move into it.
